articles.title: An Arch fleet inventory model for third-party package risk
articles.excerpt: An Arch fleet inventory model for third-party package risk The yyay incident asks a basic inventory question: which machines are allowed to build or install software from a community recipe, and who a…
articles.body: An Arch fleet inventory model for third-party package risk The yyay incident asks a basic inventory question: which machines are allowed to build or install software from a community recipe, and who approved the exact recipe that ran? A list of installed package names is a start, but it does not capture the maintainer, build source, install script, or execution context that made this case dangerous. Arch fleets need a data model that can answer those questions without collecting a mass of unrelated telemetry. The model should connect a package approval to the evidence used to grant it and to the hosts where it is allowed to run. It should also make removal and investigation possible when a public warning appears.

articles.title: $11.4 Million in NVIDIA Cargo Vanishes Aboard a Food Truck: AI Chip Theft Continues in the Bay Area
articles.excerpt: Six pallets of NVIDIA cargo worth about ¥1.8 billion vanished aboard a truck bearing a food carrier's logo. The truck left Oakland on August 29, and two months later no arrests had been made. Key poin…
articles.body: Six pallets of NVIDIA cargo worth about ¥1.8 billion vanished aboard a truck bearing a food carrier's logo. The truck left Oakland on August 29, and two months later no arrests had been made. Key points What happened: Six pallets of NVIDIA cargo worth $11.4 million (about ¥1.8 billion) disappeared in Southern California after pickup by a truck posing as a food carrier. Two months later, no arrests had been made. Why thieves target the chips: US export controls mean NVIDIA chips fetch about twice the domestic price on overseas black markets. Stolen chips can provide a way around those restrictions. What to watch: The Bay Area has seen a series of NVIDIA cargo thefts since 2025. The methods are growing more sophisticated, including GPS spoofing and carrier impersonation.

articles.title: RabbitMQ's Default Prefetch Is Unlimited. One Slow Worker Can Hoard the Whole Queue
articles.excerpt: Book: Event-Driven Architecture Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for d…
articles.body: Book: Event-Driven Architecture Pocket Guide Also by me: Thinking in Go (2-book series) — Complete Guide to Go Programming + Hexagonal Architecture in Go My project: Hermes IDE | GitHub — an IDE for developers who ship with Claude Code and other AI coding tools Me: xgabriel.com | GitHub Your deploy stops all ten workers, ships, and starts them again. While they were down, 8,000 jobs piled up in a classic queue. The first worker back opens a channel, starts consuming, and the broker pushes it the whole backlog. The other nine come up a few seconds later and find nothing to take. That first worker happens to sit on a busy node and runs at 300 ms a job, so it will need 40 minutes to get through what it holds. The management UI shows 0 ready and 8,000 unacked.

articles.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking the public to send their names to Titan for an ambitious mission that will see a flying craft explore the Saturn moon in 2034, if all goes according to plan.
articles.body: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034.

articles.excerpt: The movies might be struggling to recapture the magic, but Star Wars video games are strong with the Force.
articles.body: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences.

articles.body: Spoilers follow for Godzilla Minus Zero . Godzilla Minus Zero is upon us, and going by the reviews , it looks like the venerable kaiju franchise has another winner on its hands. More than 70 years after his debut, Godzilla continues to be one of the most iconic characters in cinema history. But even though Minus Zero is another strong entry for the King of the Monsters, I couldn’t help but be a little disappointed that the movie continues a frustrating trend that’s plagued the last couple decades of Godzilla movies by only featuring a handful of his monster co-stars. Specifically, King Ghidorah is the antagonist of Minus Zero, once again assuming his role as the Big G’s archenemy.

articles.body: From 1980 until 1995, cartoonist Gary Larson wrote and drew The Far Side . It was a single panel comic strip filled with non-sequitur, surreal jokes mostly aimed at adults instead of children, which was unusual for newspaper comics at the time. Also unusual was the fact that, unlike most daily comic strips, The Far Side had no recurring characters. Peanuts has its gang of kids and Garfield has its cast of humans and animals, but every panel of The Far Side introduces new characters and scenarios all aimed at delivering one single joke.

articles.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Nov. 6). It was the company's 125th liftoff of 2026.
articles.body: SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026.

articles.title: Starlink Mobile: All the news on SpaceX’s major mobile carrier ambitions
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challeng…
articles.body: SpaceX has declared that it’s going to make Starlink Mobile a “major” mobile carrier. The Elon Musk-owned company has already deployed thousands of direct-to-cell satellites, but its next big challenge is building out its 5G network here on Earth. As part of its plans to rival AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, SpaceX has inked a deal with Qualcomm , which will deploy its cellular technology across tens of thousands of 5G cell sites starting in 2027. SpaceX is also reportedly in talks to buy Boost Mobile , potentially allowing it to launch Starlink Mobile through the service. Another report suggests SpaceX may tap into 80,000 cell sites across the US to build out its network. SpaceX’s big plans have garnered some reactions in the telecom industry.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova later caleld the Tycho supernova with his bare eyes. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago.
